\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/robodojo-release-score.pdf}
  \caption{\textbf{Mean task score on RoboDojo-RC Tier~1 against model release date.} Each point is one model configuration (M/H/XH: medium, high and extra-high reasoning effort; UF: ultrafast serving), scored over 120 attempts (20 per task); bars are 95\% bootstrap intervals. Filled markers with bold labels are the record setters: the configurations that no configuration released on or before them beat. The dashed line is a least-squares exponential fit to the record setters ($\log_2$ of the value against release date). Its doubling time is 44.5 days: the record rose from 14.9\% (GPT-5.6 Sol~(H), July 2026) to 48.3\% (Claude Opus~5.5~(XH), September 2026).}
  \label{fig:release-score}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/robodojo-release-rate-cost.pdf}
  \caption{\textbf{Subtasks completed per hour of wall-clock time (top) and API cost per subtask (bottom) against model release date.} Rate is a configuration's summed subtasks over its 120 attempts divided by their summed duration (an attempt judged at milestone $k$ of its task completes $k$ subtasks); cost is its summed API cost divided by the same subtasks. As ratios of totals they carry no intervals. Markers are as in Figure~\ref{fig:release-score}, with record setters the fastest and the cheapest configurations to date; with only three record setters on each panel, no trend is fitted. The rate record rose from 12.4 subtasks per hour (GPT-5.6 Sol~(H), July 2026) to 54.4 (GPT-6 Astra~(H+UF), September 2026), and the cost record fell from \$2.36 per subtask (GPT-5.6 Sol~(H), July 2026) to \$0.38 (Gemini 3.8 Flash~(H), September 2026); Table~\ref{tab:release-records} gives the ranges.}
  \label{fig:release-rate-cost}
\end{figure}
